description: Fabricated Paper Out® Request inputs. The Name of Request value is invented and identifies no real batch, requester or business record. The Approver is never fabricated here - it is selected from the real, organization-configured options the Approver combobox already offers at run time.
safetyNote: TS-EC-12000-001, -002 and -004 never submit the Paper Out Request modal to completion (TS-002 stops at the Acknowledgement modal opening, TS-004 cancels it), so no real Work Queue item or transaction state is created by those three. TS-EC-12000-003, -007, -008, -009 and -010 are different by design: they perform a real submission, which IS the acceptance criterion under test, not an accidental side effect. A pending Paper Out request locks every transaction it covers, so tagged After hooks in steps/paper-out-media-type.steps.ts cancel each item again at the end of its scenario; without that the application refuses the next run with 'Cannot process paper out request. The following transactions are currently locked' (observed live 2026-09-14). Cancelling is the only non-destructive exit and only works while the request is still Submitted/Approval: approving it moves the request to Authorized/Verification where the sole remaining action is Verify, which permanently removes the source documents from the vault and would consume the fixture. Collection names are deliberately not recorded here: qa5's Collections list changed once already during this story without warning ('demo collection'/'test collection' became 'c1'..'c5'), so a name recorded as data would silently go stale the next time that happens. Eligibility is instead re-established at runtime by resolveOpenCancelCollectionName and resolveSubmittableCollectionName in steps/paper-out-media-type.steps.ts, which read whatever collections the accordion is actually offering and cache the first one that qualifies for the rest of the run. Eligibility can only be established by attempting a real submission - the modal opens and renders its full Media Type section for collections that will still be refused, so an open modal is never evidence of eligibility on its own.
